mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.25% per month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when the trigger is met in at least three out of the last five tightening episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of at least 2% coincident with a rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 6.5% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls YoY by >= 2% AND UNRATE > 6.5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) in at least four out of the last six episodes meeting the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by > 0.3pp for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during at least five out of the last seven instances when the trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of at least 0.5% for four consecutive months signals a contraction in economic output, which depresses earnings growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >= 0.5% per month for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) in at least three out of the last five contraction episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month decline in the federal funds rate by at least 0.75 percentage points signals an emergency easing in response to a financial shock, which boosts liquidity and supports equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops by >= 0.75% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) in at least two out of the last three emergency easing episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both personal savings (RSAFS) and the housing starts index (HOUST) by at least 5% month-over-month signals a shift from consumption to savings and construction, which can temporarily depress consumer discretionary spending and weigh on earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and HOUST both rise by at least 5% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) in at least three out of the last five post-recession episodes meeting the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) of at least 50,000 jobs for six consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises by at least 50,000 for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) in at least four out of the last six late-cycle expansion episodes meeting the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) of at least 3% coincident with a decline in real GDP (GDPC1) signals inflationary pressure amid weak growth, which erodes purchasing power and increases input costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL rises YoY by >= 3% AND GDPC1 falls YoY
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) in at least three out of the last five stagflation episodes meeting the trigger.
